chunks: Do you expect that Allah may give you the reward of the humble while you yourself remain vain in His view?
And do you covet that He may give you the reward of those practising charity while you enjoy comforts and deny them to the weak and the widows?
Certainly, a man is awarded according as he acts and meets what he has sent forward; and that is an end to the matter.
ai.seo_question: What is the principle of divine recompense for actions in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this epistle to the deputy governor of Basra, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the discrepancy between outward religious expectations and inner spiritual reality, highlighting how arrogance and hoarding wealth from the vulnerable negate the merit of humility and charity. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *bada'* (accountability for one's deeds) and the concept that true reward is contingent upon the sincerity and consistency of one's actions, as summarized by the phrase 'a person is judged by what he has sent ahead.' The warning underscores the transient nature of worldly ease (*na'im*) versus the eternal consequences of one's moral legacy.
